title: Quantum emitters for aerospace applications
author: Leonardo Antonio Lugarini
abstract: Key exchange via quantum key distribution (QKD) ensures cryptographic protection at the physical level, i.e., the laws of quantum mechanics guarantee the security of the channel, including protection against quantum computers, which will be capable of breaking current encryption. Key exchange via quantum distribution is done by photons and can be conducted through both optical fibers and free space. In the latter case, it can be done using satellites; for example, since 2016, China has had the Micius satellite for quantum communication, and similar missions are being planned by the USA and the EU. The initial block of a quantum communication system is single-photon sources, systems capable of sending a single photon in a stimulated manner. Quantum emitters, physical systems that behave similarly to a two-level system, approximate single-photon sources. One of the main ways to increase the efficiency of quantum emitters is through the Purcell Effect. In this undergraduate work, we will study the Purcell Effect in heterostructures designed to support surface modes that efficiently couple with quantum emitters for the desired frequency ranges.
